note: Client-safe short source windows for academy foundation sessions. Hebrew and translations are excerpts already used in this repo (or public-domain Hebrew plus a short educational gloss), so a learner can answer on the page. Sefaria links are secondary. Do not treat this as a full text store.

Genesis 1:1.hebrew: בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ
Genesis 1:1.translation: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
Genesis 1:1.setting: Opening verse of the Torah — a narrative line, not a rule or a debate.

Genesis 1:1–2:3.hebrew: בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ
Genesis 1:1–2:3.translation: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
Genesis 1:1–2:3.setting: The first creation account runs from this opening verse through the close of the seventh day.

Deuteronomy 6:4.hebrew: שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד
Deuteronomy 6:4.translation: Hear, Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord is one.
Deuteronomy 6:4.setting: A Torah verse of direct address — later reused in prayer, but first a verse.

Mishnah Berakhot 1:1.translation: From when do we recite Shema in the evening?
Mishnah Berakhot 1:1.setting: A compact Mishnah question about a practice and its time — a rule-shaped opening, not a story.

Berakhot 2a.translation: On what is the tanna standing, that he teaches: “From when?”
Berakhot 2a.setting: The Gemara quotes the Mishnah’s rule-shaped opening and immediately presses it with a question.

Berakhot 2a (Vilna page).translation: From when do we recite Shema in the evening?
Berakhot 2a (Vilna page).setting: On a Vilna Talmud page this Mishnah–Gemara block sits in the center; commentary fills the columns around it.

Mishnah and Gemara, Berakhot 2a.translation: From when do we recite Shema in the evening?
Mishnah and Gemara, Berakhot 2a.setting: The Mishnah states the practice; the Gemara that follows (often marked גמ׳) begins the discussion of it.

Gemara Berakhot 2a.translation: On what is the tanna standing, that he teaches: “From when?”
Gemara Berakhot 2a.setting: A Gemara line that asks about the Mishnah’s opening rather than retelling a story.

Mikraot Gedolot, Genesis 1:1.hebrew: בְּרֵאשִׁית בָּרָא אֱלֹהִים אֵת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ
Mikraot Gedolot, Genesis 1:1.translation: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
Mikraot Gedolot, Genesis 1:1.setting: On a Mikraot Gedolot page the verse sits as the primary text; commentaries are printed around it.

Pirkei Avot 1:1.hebrew: מֹשֶׁה קִבֵּל תּוֹרָה מִסִּינַי וּמְסָרָהּ לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ
Pirkei Avot 1:1.translation: Moses received the Torah at Sinai and handed it to Joshua.
Pirkei Avot 1:1.setting: An anonymous Mishnah voice narrating a chain of transmission — no “Rabbi X said” formula on this opening line.

Pirkei Avot 1:2.hebrew: שִׁמְעוֹן הַצַּדִּיק הָיָה מִשְּׁיָרֵי כְנֶסֶת הַגְּדוֹלָה. הוּא הָיָה אוֹמֵר
Pirkei Avot 1:2.translation: Shimon the Righteous was of the remnants of the Great Assembly. He used to say…
Pirkei Avot 1:2.setting: A named sage plus “he used to say” — an attribution formula before the teaching itself.

Kaddish.translation: May His great name be magnified and sanctified.
Kaddish.setting: A prayer of public praise — liturgical address, not a legal case or a Torah narrative.

Rambam, Yesodei HaTorah 1:1.hebrew: יְסוֹד הַיְסוֹדוֹת וְעַמּוּד הַחָכְמוֹת לֵידַע שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם מָצוּי רִאשׁוֹן
Rambam, Yesodei HaTorah 1:1.translation: The foundation of foundations and the pillar of wisdoms is to know that there is a First Being.
Rambam, Yesodei HaTorah 1:1.setting: A code-style claim stated as a principle, not as a back-and-forth sugya.
